clips.text: The Eckington boys, who have not many victories to their credit, stepped out to capture two games.
This will be the last meeting of the guild until January, but the guild office in Sibley Hospital will be open every day except Saturday, with Mrs. H. S. France in charge.
Charles W. Mason, 79 years old, for 30 years employed as a clerk for the, firm of Barber Ross, hardware dealers, died in Sibley Hospital Sun day after a long illness.
The speaker also predicted that the Retail and farmers’ market would not r> at Eckington, but near the middle of the city.

The retail and farmers’ sections of the market, he said, should go to a cen tral location, near the old Convention Hall, and the large wholesale concerns should be located in Eckington. where trackage facilities would be available.
… Fates street suffered a fracture of the skull and minor injuries about 4 o’clock yesterday afternoon, when struck by a street car while crossing in front of 1407 North Capitol street.

note: Clips are machine-read text (OCR) from scanned Evening Star pages on the Library of Congress's Chronicling America, lightly cleaned (line-break hyphens rejoined, stray symbols removed); misspellings are the scanner's. Newspapers this old are public domain. Each clip links to its page at loc.gov. Clips that mention race, covenants, deed restrictions or slurs are skipped automatically (keyword list: race, races, racial, colored, coloured, negro, negroes, white only, whites only, for whites, white people, white persons, white residents, caucasian, segregation, segregated, covenant, covenants, restricted, restriction, restrictions, plus a list of slurs), because they need an editor's context; legal notices and lists of private individuals are skipped too.
